Customer Record Maintenance
Centralized Revenue Model
Client Retention Metrics
questions.explain: CRM is Customer Relationship Management — both the software and the practice of tracking every interaction with prospects and customers.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what makes CRM software actually useful to a business?
options: Having the most expensive CRM license available
The software combined with the discipline of actually using it, not the software alone
Only sales reps are allowed to see any of the data
Replacing every spreadsheet with a single printed binder
questions.explain: The lesson states that software without the discipline of using it is just an expensive, out-of-date address book — both halves matter.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of what breaks without a shared CRM system, according to this lesson?
options: The office printer runs out of toner
A customer's invoice is one day late
A deal gets double-worked or dropped entirely when the rep handling it is out sick
The company website briefly goes offline
questions.explain: Without visibility into where things stood, nobody else can pick up a deal when the rep who owned it is unavailable.

questions.q: What does "system of record" mean, as used in this lesson?
options: A backup copy of data that is rarely checked
A spreadsheet one employee keeps for personal reference
A system used only to record audio calls
The one place a business trusts as the accurate, current version of a piece of information
questions.explain: A system of record is the trusted, shared source of truth — not a personal or scattered copy.

questions.q: Why does this course teach the concept of CRM before teaching Salesforce the product?
options: Because Salesforce is not actually a CRM platform
Because understanding the underlying job makes the tool's buttons and settings make sense, instead of memorizing clicks with no context
Because the concept of CRM has nothing to do with Salesforce
Because Chapter 3 replaces the need to learn the concept at all
questions.explain: The lesson explains that every feature Salesforce ships serves the same underlying CRM job, so understanding that job first gives the later software lessons real context.
